question: Should experimental Claw bundles be allowed to install globally named MCP declarations, and if so what host authorization, command broker, and sharing scope must be enforced before they reach the shared MCP config?
rationale: The patch creates persistent authority over executable and remote MCP configuration, while current policy favors explicit operator control and avoids duplicating existing plugin or MCP paths; source inspection cannot choose the permanent trust model safely.

options.title: Require a brokered, host-authorized model
options.body: Accept the direction only after manifest commands pass an approved broker or allowlist and every shared declaration has explicit host authorization.

options.title: Limit Claws to non-executable references
options.body: Permit Claws to reference existing host-managed MCP declarations but prohibit bundle-driven creation of commands or remote endpoints.

options.title: Defer the lifecycle owner
options.body: Keep this stack unmerged while the RFC decides whether bundle-style plugins rather than core Claw state should own MCP installation.

recommendation.title: Require a brokered, host-authorized model
recommendation.body: Accept the direction only after manifest commands pass an approved broker or allowlist and every shared declaration has explicit host authorization.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision directly affects the shared MCP configuration contract whose current history is attributed to vincentkoc.
